final_answer:
The top predicted non-MHC-I communication programs from celiac-enriched KIR+ cytotoxic CD8 T cells to activated/memory CD4 T cells were CCL5 chemokine signaling, LGALS1/galectin-1 signaling, TGF-beta-associated signaling, and contact/apoptosis pathways involving CD58-CD2, CD47-SIRPG, and FASLG-FAS.

In the celiac-only LIANA consensus analysis, the strongest non-MHC edge was CCL5->CCR4 (empirical p < 0.002; specificity_rank=0.000105), with additional CCL5->CXCR3 and CCL5->DPP4 interactions. This supports chemokine-mediated colocalization or retention of activated CD4 targets near KIR+ CD8 cells. The next strongest program was LGALS1/galectin-1 signaling, especially LGALS1->ITGB1 (p < 0.002; specificity_rank=0.000339; magnitude_rank=0.122418), with LGALS1->CD69 and LGALS1->PTPRC also detected, consistent with suppressive or pro-apoptotic regulation of activated T cells. TGFB1-associated interactions, led by TGFB1->ITGB1 (p < 0.002; specificity_rank=0.025332), suggest an additional immunoregulatory/tissue-retention axis.

For cytotoxic targeting, FASLG->FAS was predicted (p < 0.002; specificity_rank=0.036142), but it was low-abundance, with FASLG detected in 8.9% of KIR+ CD8 cells and FAS in 13.5% of activated CD4 cells, so it is a plausible but not dominant mechanism. CD58->CD2 and CD47->SIRPG were also significant and may stabilize T-cell contact, enabling granule-mediated killing by the NKG7/GNLY/GZMB/PRF1-high KIR+ CD8 population. IFNG->IFNGR1_IFNGR2 was significant but much less specific (specificity_rank=0.415913), and TRAIL/TNFSF10 death-receptor signaling was not supported.

Thus, beyond the established MHC-I interaction, the most defensible candidate pathways are CCL5-mediated recruitment/retention, LGALS1/galectin-1-mediated suppression, TGFB1-mediated immunoregulation, CD58-CD2/CD47-SIRPG contact stabilization, and a weaker FASLG-FAS apoptotic axis. The activated CD4 population is only a transcriptomic proxy for pathogenic gliadin-specific CD4 T cells; antigen specificity and functional killing cannot be proven from these scRNA-seq ligand-receptor data alone.
